breakdown_notes: Paper: Blanchard & Katz, 'Regional Evolutions', Brookings Papers on Economic Activity 1992 (75 pp.). It reports NO hardware, NO wall-clock training/inference time, NO API costs, and NO GPU usage -- as expected for a 1992 econometrics paper that predates code/data archiving (the only 'computer' reference in the text is Wang Laboratories cited as an example firm in Lowell, MA). All quantitative work is classical small-panel econometrics on 50 states + DC (51 cross-sectional units) over ~1947-1990 (~40 annual observations each): OLS cross-sectional persistence/convergence regressions, per-state ADF unit-root tests (4 lags + trend), pooled fixed-effects AR models, and low-order (2-4 lag) bivariate/trivariate VARs with impulse responses. Periods of estimation quoted in the paper: '1952-90 for employment and wages and 1972-90 for unemployment' (Table 1 note); state-national elasticities use 1948-90 (Alaska 1961-90, Hawaii 1956-90). Datasets are tiny (a few thousand state-year rows, a handful of MB) and every model is closed-form or a small least-squares/VAR fit that runs in well under a second; the full replication analysis executes in seconds of CPU. No GPU is required for any step and no external LLM API is called on any sample. The replication plan (10 steps) confirms this: step 1 is env setup, step 2 rebuilds the panel by fetching public series over the internet (BLS CES/SAE, BLS LAUS, BEA Regional accounts, FRED), and steps 3-10 are the CPU-bound econometric analyses. The only non-trivial wall-clock cost is network I/O during data acquisition (BLS/BEA/FRED API and flat-file downloads) plus a one-time pip install -- both bandwidth/latency bound, not compute bound, and typically a few minutes. Because raw compute is sub-5-minute CPU with no GPU/LLM, compute_class is 'light'. Note: several claims (C25/C27/C28/C31/C33/C34) are blocked in the plan because they depend on proprietary privately-supplied series (NAR metro house prices, Davis-Loungani-Mahidhara defense contracts, Bartik instrument) that are not reconstructable; those do not change the compute profile.
estimated_cost_source: No paid compute required: CPU-only classical econometrics; no GPU rental and no paid LLM/API calls. Public data sources (BLS, BEA, FRED) are free.
estimated_runs_notes: Not ML runs/seeds. Most analyses loop the same estimator over the 51 state units (e.g. per-state ADF tests, per-state employment elasticities, per-state univariate long-run responses). Deterministic OLS/VAR fits -- no random seeds, so no multi-seed averaging.
dataset_size_notes: State-level annual panel: 51 units x ~40 years across a handful of series (employment, manufacturing wages, personal income, population, unemployment/labor force). On the order of a few thousand rows and a few MB total -- fits easily in memory.
internet_notes: Required only for data acquisition (BLS CES/SAE & LAUS, BEA Regional API/SAINC1/CA1, FRED). The paper itself does not archive data; the plan reconstructs it from public endpoints. Pre-1976 state unemployment (a privately-supplied constructed LMA series) is not reconstructable.
parallelizable_notes: The independent per-state regressions/ADF tests/VARs are embarrassingly parallel, but the workload is so small that serial execution already finishes in seconds; parallelism is unnecessary.
estimated_wallclock_notes: Dominated by network data downloads and one pip install; the econometric computation is seconds.
